recipes.name: Tomato, Corn, and Avocado Salsa
ingredients_raw: 1 (11 ounce) can whole kernel corn, drained
1 (4 ounce) can sliced black olives, drained
1 red bell pepper, seeded and diced

steps.text: Mix together corn, olives, tomatoes, onion, red pepper, and jalapeño pepper in a large bowl until well combined. Gently fold in avocados, olive oil, lime juice, and salt.

raw_recipe.headline: Tomato, Corn, and Avocado Salsa
raw_recipe.description: Fresh tomatoes, corn, and avocado combine in this colorful salsa recipe, which is seasoned with lime juice and onions. Serve with your favorite chips.

video.description: This salsa is quick and easy to make. It's colorful and most important, it's delicious! Corn, avocado, pepper, olives, and other fresh and tasty ingredients mixed up in a light olive oil and lime juice are a wonderful side dish for your next dinner party! It’s refreshing and filling. For extra pizazz serve with tortilla chips!

review.reviewBody: I can't stop eating this salsa. It is super addicting. This stuff is awesome!!! Only things that I did differently was that I added 1/2 tsp. garlic salt, 1/2 tsp. sea salt, and I added a tbsp. more lime juice, and I substituted the black olives with a can of black beans b/c my husband hates olives, unfortunately. I'm surprised more people have not reviewed this outstanding recipe b/c it's THAT GOOD!

Fresh, Fresh and Perfectly Fresh Salsa! This salsa is perfect for almost any occasion such as appetizer, celebratory potluck dish, or like today a Sunday brunch starter! I did switch up the recipe a tad by: • Cutting all the ingredients the same size and using amounts similar in size. Most were 1 cup • Used grapeseed oil vs olive oil – seemed like a better flavor profile to me • I diced the avocado inside the skin and scooped out the pieces leaving the avocado skin halved • Filled the salsa mixture into the avocado skin half • Garnished with Maldon salt and small lime wedges We enjoyed this salsa with tortilla chips but it would also be amazing over a white fish, salmon, in a salad. The yummy possibilities might just be endless. My husband said “it tastes even better that is looks.”

Instead of canned corn, I cooked 4 ears of fresh corn in the microwave and cut it from the cobs. I added a large can of black beans, drained and rinsed. I also used 1.5 t garlic powder and 2 t cumin. I doubled the lime juice to 4 T. This is an excellent salsa! I will definitely make it again.

I've made this a couple times now and it is very good. I was asked for the recipe at the potluck and that has never happened to me before. The only things I do differently are to use cherry or grape tomatoes instead of roma, add an extra avocado, and add cilantro. To me, it just isn't salsa without cilantro! **Update 10/15/11** I am no longer permitted to attend any potluck without bringing this dish! No matter how much I make, there is never any left. The secret to making this the best ever, is to combine all the ingredients except the avocado the night before and refrigerate. This allows the flavors to meld into perfection. The avocado will turn mushy if you add them the night before. Also make sure to cover it tightly otherwise the strong onion smell will permeate your entire fridge!

I've made this as stated as well as a fancier version using fresh corn from the cob and chopped kalamata olives instead of the canned. The latter version is more time consuming, but the fresh corn and added flavor from the kalamatas brings it to another level. I only added a 1/4 cup of diced kalamatas - you don't need as much because they have 10x the flavor of canned olives. The recipe as stated is also good and a lot quicker!

I made a few changes as well. I sauteed 4 ears of fresh corn in olive oil with kosher salt. Replaced the olives with a can of black beans. Used 6 small tomatoes, one red and one orange bell pepper, 2 avocados and 2 Tablespoons minced jalapenos. the juice from 4 limes. It was a huge hit!
I mixed everything except avocado ahead of time to let flavors mingle. I also added black beans. When ready to serve I cut up two avocados. Nice fresh texture and flavor. I served with scoops.
Won grand prize at 49er pre-season opener at Levi Stadium 2014! Minor alterations. 1) More Jalapeno (seeded) 2) Fresh White corn grilled instead of can. 3) 75% more lime juice 4) Marinaded over night

This is really delicious - even better with fresh corn & cilantro! I usually grill the corn to give it that little hint of smokiness. I use canned if I'm in a rush but if I have time, we find that the fresh-grilled corn and a little cilantro just takes this salsa over the top! Try it!
I added a can of black beans(rinsed). It took it to another level. Have had it as a salsa, salad, and in a wrap. Very pleased!

Great recipe. Like others, I substituted the olives with black beans and added the avocado when it was time to serve it. Seasoned it with additional spices (cumin, paprika, onion powder, garlic powder, cayenne). Let it marinade for a few hours. Great flavor - very fresh, healthy. I served it with chips or as a side to our meal.
This was amazing! The only thing I did different was, I chopped really tiny a couple of jarred jalapeño slices! This recipe is refreshing on a hot day! A keeper!!
It was yummy! I added Black Beans instead of Olives and only added 2 tomatoes without the insides. Also, added extra lime/lemon juice for more zip to the flavor.
Like someone else, did we swapped out the black olives for black beans. This was super easy to make and is delicious!
Loved it! added more jalapeno, Perfect!
Made as stated and got a thumbs up from family and friends.

I think black beans would be a nice addition. Does not keep long with avocados turning brown quickly.
Flavor was good.

This is delicious. I made it for a party and everyone loved it. 
The colors and flavors are wonderful.
Definitely a keeper. Loved it! Just added a few spices to make it my own.
